# v2.53-dev Release Notes

## Compliance Planning: clearer wording, scope-consistent requirements, and accurate tier totals

### Changed

- **"People-moves" / "moves" is now "People to certify".** The headline number
  on Compliance Planning was hard to read at a glance. It's now labelled
  **People to certify** everywhere — the KPI card, each program's summary, and
  the per-specialisation cost — because that's exactly what it counts: how many
  people still need to earn a certification to close the gaps (deduplicated, so
  one person whose single exam satisfies several requirements counts once).

- **Planning a country no longer pulls in the theatre above it.** Each scope now
  plans against **only its own-level requirements**, exactly like the program
  dashboards. Choosing a country shows that country's requirements; the wider
  theatre-level requirement is only shown when you actually select the theatre.
  The old "shared" tag has been removed.

### Fixed

- **Tier plans now cost only the cheapest path, not the whole program.** Aiming
  at a tier reported a wildly inflated number (it was adding up the gap for
  *every* specialisation in the program, even though reaching the tier only
  needs a few). It now counts just the cheapest specialisation(s) actually
  required to reach the tier — so a tier that needs one more specialisation
  costing two people now reads **2 people to certify**, not the whole program's
  backlog.

- **Double-counting at country scope is gone.** A requirement that existed at
  both country and theatre level was being counted twice (once for the country,
  once for the theatre-wide copy). With each scope showing only its own-level
  requirements, each gap is counted once.

- **Equally-cheap specialisations are no longer hidden.** When two (or more)
  specialisations are tied as the cheapest way to reach a tier, the plan now
  flags **all** of them **Recommended** (with an "achieve any N" note) instead
  of silently naming only the first. Non-recommended specialisations are still
  shown, dimmed, for reference.

### Notes

- No database migration and no configuration required.
- Compliance Planning is a live view — it always reflects current data.
